extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent attorneys, and KIPO examiners (parties before the Korean Intellectual Property Office and the IP Trial & Appeal Board)
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural rules governing interruption, suspension, resumption, submission, electronic filing, and service of documents in patent-related proceedings before the Korean Intellectual Property Office and the Intellectual Property Trial and Appeal Board. Focuses on who may act, timing/effective dates, examiner duties, and methods of service and electronic submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resumption of interrupted proceeding
rubrics_metrics.description: When a proceeding was interrupted, a person entitled may request resumption; the Commissioner or administrative patent judge shall determine whether to permit resumption and may dismiss a request if no grounds exist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Request for resumption must be in writing and include evidential documents of grounds; the Commissioner/administrative patent judge shall notify opposing parties of the request; if a person required to resume fails to do so, the Commissioner/judge may order resumption within a specified period and if not resumed the proceeding shall be deemed resumed the day after expiration; notifications to all relevant parties are required; Commissioner/judge may determine separately when a certified copy of a decision was served. The Commissioner/judge shall dismiss groundless requests based on ex officio investigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspension of proceeding (natural disaster/indefinite impediment)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proceedings may be suspended when the Commissioner or an administrative patent judge is unable to perform duties due to natural disaster or other extenuating circumstances, or where a party faces impediments of indefinite duration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suspension under these grounds continues until circumstances cease; Commissioner/judge may order suspension by decision for party impediments (examples: communications disrupted by war; party suddenly ill and unable to contact KIPO); the Commissioner/judge may revoke suspension decisions and must notify all relevant parties when suspending or revoking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of interruption or suspension on running of periods
rubrics_metrics.description: When a patent-related proceeding is interrupted or suspended, the running of the relevant period is interrupted, and the entire period restarts from the time the resumption/continuation is notified or the proceeding is resumed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The elapsed time before interruption/suspension is not counted; the full statutory or designated period recommences upon resumption. Example: if a one-month amendment period had 15 days elapsed before interruption, after resumption the applicant has the full one month again. In principle, while interrupted/suspended, KIPO/examiner shall not proceed with the matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinction between interruption and suspension (definitions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Interruption: discontinuation because a party involved cannot conduct the proceeding (e.g., death, loss of capacity). Suspension: discontinuation because KIPO or a party cannot proceed (natural disaster, extenuating circumstances) or by KIPO decision for indefinite obstacles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interruption arises from legal reasons irrespective of parties' intentions; suspension may be automatic (KIPO unable to carry out duties) or by decision (party impediment). The rules determine who may resume and how proceedings are handled once grounds arise or cease.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may resume an interrupted proceeding (succession and capacity)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific categories of persons may resume interrupted proceedings: successors in title, administrators of inherited property, juristic persons continuing after merger, persons who recovered capacity, newly become legal representatives, newly-appointed trustees, new representatives where prior representative deceased or disqualified, persons with same qualification as trustee in bankruptcy, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A successor in title may not resume until he/she renounces inheritance; example references Article 1019 Civil Act for acceptance/renunciation periods. The list (①–⑦) specifies substituting parties who can request resumption based on the particular ground for interruption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure and evidentiary requirements for resumption requests
rubrics_metrics.description: A resumption must be requested in writing stating intention and attaching evidential documents of the grounds for resumption; requests are submitted to the Commissioner or presiding administrative patent judge who will notify the opposing party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Opposing party can request the Commissioner/judge to order the party to file a resumption request pursuant to Article 21 paragraphs; the Commissioner/judge shall dismiss groundless resumption requests after ex officio investigation; when resumption is ordered and not complied with, the proceeding may be deemed resumed after a designated period and parties are notified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner duties on awareness of interruption/resumption grounds
rubrics_metrics.description: Generally, an examiner conducts examination without separately investigating interruption unless made aware; if the Commissioner becomes aware of an interruption ground during examination the examiner shall suspend the examination until resumption.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If examiner becomes aware of grounds for resumption, he/she shall order resumption within a designated period in the name of the Commissioner and notify the party; if a resumption request is not filed within the designated period it is deemed filed and the examiner shall notify and proceed. If an examiner overlooks an interruption ground and continues, the proceeding shall be invalidated and re-conducted from the beginning. Example: an examiner issuing a notice of grounds for rejection while applicant died — the rejection is illegitimate; the examiner must revoke and provide opportunity after resumption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective date of submission of documents (general rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: An application, request, or other document submitted to the Commissioner or President takes effect from the date it reaches them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If submitted by post, effective date is the date stamped by postal authority if clear, otherwise date evidenced by postal receipt; if neither, date delivered to KIPO. Special rules apply for applications for registration and international applications: postal submissions of such documents take effect on the date received by KIPO (not merely postage stamp date). Matters for delay, loss, interruption of postal service to be prescribed by Ordinance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective date rules for international applications and postal delays
rubrics_metrics.description: Documents for international applications (PCT) submitted by mail take effect on the date received by KIPO; delays or loss in international phase handled per Enforcement Rules Articles 86/87 or applicable PCT Rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where PCT Rules provide differently, the PCT Rules apply preferentially. For internal applications, Enforcement Rules Articles 86/87 apply in events of mail delay or loss.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic filing: permitted methods and validity
rubrics_metrics.description: Persons may prepare patent applications and other documents in electronic form per Ordinance and submit via information/communications network or electronic recording medium; electronic documents are as valid as paper documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Electronic submissions via network are deemed received as the contents recorded in KIPO's electronic information processing system when the submitter can confirm the filing number through the network. The kinds of documents that may be submitted electronically, methods, and necessary matters are prescribed by Ordinance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting use of electronic documents and digital signature requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: A person who intends to conduct proceedings using electronic documents must report such use to the Commissioner/President and affix his/her digital signature on electronic documents to identify the submitter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Electronic documents with a digital signature are deemed submitted by the person whose digital signature is affixed; procedures for reporting and methods of affixing digital signature to be prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations and excluded documents for electronic submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain kinds of documents are excluded from electronic submission (e.g., submission of attached articles/electronic attachments, request for correction and issuance, certain documents for international applications prepared in Japanese including Annexed Forms No.35 and No.51 original copies, request for ruling under Article 214(1), and correction of digitized contents).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants filing national defense secrecy applications cannot file electronically until secrecy canceled; when electronic recording medium is used, a written submission of attached articles (Annexed Form No.7) must be submitted for documents that cannot be submitted electronically. The Ordinance prescribes specific kinds and methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure when online submission omits required attachments
rubrics_metrics.description: If online submission omits some required documents, the applicant must attach the missing documents to 'a submission of articles such as attached electronic documents' (Annexed Form No.7) within three days after confirming the receipt number and submit them in writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This ensures completeness when some documents cannot be attached during the online filing; specified three-day deadline counted from confirmation of receipt number.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deemed receipt rule for electronic notifications/service
rubrics_metrics.description: Notification or service of documents via information/communications network to persons who reported use of electronic documents is as valid as written service and is deemed received when the addressee accesses the document via their electronic system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commissioner, President, presiding administrative patent judge, administrative patent judge, or examiner may give notice/service via network; details on kinds and methods of such notification/service are prescribed by Ordinance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Which documents are subject to formal service and available service methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Documents affecting gain or loss of a patent right are subject to formal service (examples: certified copy of decision to grant a patent, notification of invalidation under Article 16(2), certified copy of decision under Article 214(3)). Methods include personal service, service by mail (registered), and service by publication per Enforcement Decree Article 18.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documents other than those specified are to be prescribed by the Commissioner; however operational practice currently treats certain non-subject documents the same as subject-to-service documents; where examination results affect right changes, use of the Government Electronic Document System (On-nara) is required. Special service procedures apply for rulings/decisions on trial, retrial or revocation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personal service requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Personal service means handing documents to the party or their representative in person and obtaining a receipt stating date and recipient's name.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner shall obtain receipt or, alternatively, have recipient write date and name on document service registry (Annexed Form No.3) or registry of postage payment by addressee (Annexed Form No.4) at dispatch box and confirm with registered seal. If recipient is not a patent attorney, both the patent attorney’s registered seal and representative’s seal must be stamped.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service by publication procedure and effective dates
rubrics_metrics.description: When domicile or place of business of a person is unknown, service by publication in the Patent Gazette may be made stating the document is available for delivery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Initial service by publication takes effect two weeks after date of publication; subsequent service by publication to the same party takes effect the day after publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service on overseas residents
rubrics_metrics.description: Documents to overseas residents shall be served on their appointed patent administrator if one exists; otherwise they may be posted by registered airmail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documents posted by registered airmail are deemed served on the mailing date of the documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conducting multiple concurrent patent-related proceedings submitted by different media
rubrics_metrics.description: Where two or more proceedings are required to be conducted at the same time by ordinance and are submitted online, they shall be entered consecutively; if one is online and others are submitted by electronic recording medium or in writing, all concerned proceedings shall be conducted on the same day.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This ensures synchronized processing when multiple related proceedings are filed via different submission methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuation of proceeding and succession of effect upon transfer of rights
rubrics_metrics.description: When a patent right or patent-related right is transferred while a proceeding is pending, the Commissioner or presiding administrative patent judge may require the successor in title to continue the proceeding; the effect of the already-initiated proceeding reaches the successor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proceeding does not need to commence anew after transfer; example: if notice of change of applicant filed within designated period after notification of grounds for rejection, examiner need not resend notification to successor and the period for submission of written argument remains the original designated period.
